limits: One optimizer seed and eight adaptive development scenarios; no algorithm-level inference, formal selection or held-out confirmation.
All sixteen rollout curves and null explained-variance values are retained in external mechanism evidence; this compact record contains full-curve summaries, not selected-time substitutes.
The deterministic first 256 env-major buffer samples are pre-update diagnostics, not shuffled SGD minibatches or Adam parameter updates. The final diagnostic precedes the final optimization.
Common actor-plus-reward-critic clipping factors are implied by the diagnostic minibatch. They do not prove the actual cumulative actor update.

Training reward MSE uses scaled units; dividing by reward_scale squared restores units but does not make different states or bootstrap targets comparable. Explained variance is undefined when target variance is zero.
Reward-return diagnostics are bootstrapped lambda returns; ledger reward_return is a sum of immediate scaled training rewards, not weekly evaluation value.
PI and scalar ledger approximate KL differ in aggregation; cross-family KL is not a matched optimizer statistic.

Checkpoint, ledger and source custody verified. Diagnostic file hashes and step/multiplier joins are recorded; diagnostic files are not embedded cryptographic commitments in the final checkpoint payload.
All controller failures remain explicit incomplete slots with null weekly aggregates. Physical prefix replay cannot independently authenticate the controller exception.
Observed startup-energy and fault-response associations identify engineering hypotheses; no counterfactual repair was run in batch 001.

evidence: E expected clipped-coordinate fraction is about 2.63e-7 to 5.75e-7 over all sixteen snapshots; sampled observed fraction is zero throughout.
B expected clipped-coordinate fraction remains about .306-.321.
E exceeds B in service and EUR on all eight development scenarios; its average service is 90.53%.
E is still economically worse on average than H and OperatingMPC, passes strict safety on 0/8 and all daily returns on 0/8.
low_initial_std.finding: Lower initial standard deviation nearly removes sampled action-space clipping and markedly improves final control versus broad-std PI; feasibility and economic competitiveness remain unproven.
low_initial_std.interpretation: Supports initial exploration/clipping as relevant to the failure; it changes visited states, entropy and gradients together, so clipping alone is not isolated.

operational_benefit.reason: No PPO arm passes strict safety or all daily resource returns in any of the eight development cases; the strongest service arm E has worse mean EUR than the strong H and OperatingMPC baselines.

evidence: PI is operationally better than scalar with raw reward, but worse with scaled reward, in all eight matched cases for each contrast.
Weighted cost actor norm is larger than reward actor norm on average, but aggregate gradient cosines are negative in only 7/16 A, 5/16 B and 1/16 E diagnostics.
PI multipliers end near 1.0-1.28 without upper/lower saturation; cost EV at final diagnostic spans roughly .89-.99.
Scalar C also accumulates a mean 1799.8 kg H2, so accumulation is not exclusive to PI.
pi_signal_balance.finding: An interaction with reward conditioning, not evidence that PI alone causes accumulation or that multiplier growth exploded.
pi_signal_balance.interpretation: Constraint gradient tradeoffs and policy-dependent states remain relevant; no causal claim from gradient correlation alone.

evidence: Both raw reward arms finish with effectively zero reward EV and 100% second-layer tanh saturation in the diagnostic sample.
B and D improve reward EV over raw comparators in rollouts 2-16, but have worse initial EV.
Every paired scaled diagnostic increases clipped actor gradient norm; all 80 diagnostics still apply common clipping.
B is worse than A in service and EUR on all eight development scenarios; D is better than C on all eight.
reward_conditioning.finding: Strong support for the reward-critic conditioning diagnosis, with contradictory operational response across PI and scalar.
reward_conditioning.interpretation: Conditioning improvement is measured; a universal scaling-only operational remedy is rejected by B versus A.

confounders: Comparison uses one optimizer seed and adaptive development scenarios. E was identified after viewing the five arms.
Neither H nor OperatingMPC meets all strict daily returns. OperatingMPC consumes nearly all initial CO2 and may trade resource restoration for service value.
Greater mean delivered methane is not dominance: E has one delivery loss versus H and four versus OperatingMPC across the eight scenarios.
hypotheses: A feasibility-aware start/stop/standby prior may address persistent positive electrolysis commands during insufficient startup energy. This is a prospective experiment, not a proved counterfactual.
A structured or residual controller with an inventory-aware DAC prior may reduce unnecessary carbon capture and reliance on guard outage correction.
A separate action mapping for startup, standby and running regimes may be easier to learn than crossing their discontinuities with continuous Gaussian absolute commands.
observations: E increases mean delivered methane versus H by 171.497 kg and versus OperatingMPC by 21.960 kg, but decreases net value by EUR 1,924.01 and EUR 7,624.79 respectively.
All eight E scenarios have forced stops. All 56 daily battery and H2 returns fail, 52 daily CH4 returns fail, and one CO2 return fails.
All 88 E forced stops occur at dawn or evening; 69 also abort startup, and 86 reach SOC <= 0.151 within the interval.
E holds a nonzero DAC target throughout all 4,503 declared outage minutes; the guard drops allocations for 334.625 minutes per week.
E runs near half load almost constantly: 82.63125 low-load hours of 86.06875 operating hours weekly; this incurs more wear and battery cycling than the baselines.
